body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), uniformly over observed laws \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)\to1\) and \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}\Pr_P(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\). On \(\{\widehat T_n\ge T_0\}\), \(b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))=o_P(a(T_n(P)))\) and \(a(\widehat T_n)/a(T_n(P))\to1\). Hence the eventual-regime analytic critical value \(\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\), built from the exact Palm-intensity expansion, and the canonical-simulation critical value \(\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\), built from \(n^2\) copies of the prescribed padded grid target, satisfy \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\) and \(\Pr_P\{S_n(\theta)\le\widehat q^{\mathrm{sim}}_{n,\alpha}\}\to1-\alpha\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\); both critical values equal \(+\infty\) on the vanishing complement \(\{\widehat T_n<T_0\}\).
body.justification: Pointwise pivotality does not remove the population-dependent number of effective LR opportunities, so the spatial clock must be estimated at the centering scale.
body.gap: Takatsu and Westling (2025) estimate ingredients for Gaussian uniform bands, and Westling, Gilbert, and Carone (2020) study a pointwise isotonic scale; neither propagates a plug-in LR clock through Gumbel centering.
body.consumer: Clock substitution calculus is conditional; nominal feasible calibration is not established.

obligation.what_is_open: Calibration remains conditional on the unresolved uniform clock plug-in theorem, canonical Gumbel law, observed-law statistical transfer, random-horizon padded-grid approximation, and quantile anti-concentration.
obligation.obstruction: Relative clock consistency can control substitution into centering and scale but cannot create the missing limiting law or equate finite padded simulation quantiles with continuum quantiles.
obligation.attempted: The uniform positive volume lower bound, inverse-centering mean-value expansion, scale substitution, and conditional empirical-distribution error for \(n^2\) simulations were derived.
obligation.partial_result:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), normalization of \(p\) and strict overlap imply \(f(a)\ge c_g\) on \(J\).  The slope and variance bounds therefore give
\[
\mathcal V(P)
\ge |J|\left\{\frac{c_gc_\theta^2}{4V_\kappa}\right\}^{1/3}>0,
\]
so \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\to\infty\).  If the unresolved plug-in result supplies
\[
\widehat{\mathcal V}_n/\mathcal V(P)=1+o_P(1),
\]
then \(\log\{\widehat T_n/T_n(P)\}=o_P(1)\) and \(\Pr_P(\widehat T_n\ge T_0)\to1\) uniformly.  On that event, the mean-value theorem applied to \(\mathcal E_\star(b(T))=\log T\) yields
\[
\frac{b(\widehat T_n)-b(T_n(P))}{a(T_n(P))}
=\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
{\mathcal E_\star'(\widetilde b_n)}
\log\frac{\widehat T_n}{T_n(P)}=o_P(1),
\]
where \(\widetilde b_n\) lies between the two centerings.  Since
\[
\mathcal E_\star'(u)=\beta_\star+\frac{\gamma_\star}{u}
\]
and both centerings diverge,
\[
\frac{a(\widehat T_n)}{a(T_n(P))}
=\frac{\mathcal E_\star'(b(T_n(P)))}
{\mathcal E_\star'(b(\widehat T_n))}\longrightarrow1.
\]
Thus an established uniform Gumbel law would pass to the analytic plug-in critical value by Slutsky's theorem.  Conditionally on the data, the Dvoretzky--Kiefer--Wolfowitz inequality for the \(n^2\) simulated maxima gives empirical-distribution error \(O_P(n^{-1})\); quantile validity still requires the unresolved padded-grid approximation, random-horizon uniformity, and limiting anti-concentration.
